newsitem.title: USA: Dean Foods sees strong results in fiscal '97.
newsitem.headline: Dean Foods sees strong results in fiscal '97.

text.p: Dean Foods Co, which reported higher fiscal 1997 second quarter earnings, said it expects strong results for the balance of the year.

"We look forward to solid performance in the remainder of the year as operations extend their strong performance of the first half and we begin to realize some benefits of the cost efficiency programs initiated in our strategic review," said Howard Dean, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.

Dean Foods, a food and dairy processor and distributor of branded and private label products, reported earnings for its fiscal second quarter ended November 24 rose to $0.47 a share from $0.40 a year ago. Sales increased to $775.7 million from $705.4 million last year.

In its fiscal 1997 first half, Dean Foods earned $0.92 a share. For all of fiscal 1996, the company reported a loss of $1.24 a share after a $2.44 a share restructuring charge. The charge covered closure or disposition of 13 plants and the elimination of 840 jobs.
Earnings from vegetables, pickles and specialty segments all exceeded last year's second quarter results, while the dairy segment performance was below last year, as expected, Dean said.

The dairy segment, which benefited from changes in raw milk costs in both the first quarter of 1997 and the second quarter of 1996, was negatively affected by such changes during the second quarter this year, he said.
Dean Foods said its vegetables business showed its first quarter-over-quarter increase since fiscal 1995 as a result of increased efficiencies and an improved summer harvest.
"We continue to be extremely pleased with our fiscal 1997 results, especially with the turnaround in our vegetables segment and the strength of our pickles and specialty businesses," Dean said.
Shares of Dean Foods rose 2-1/8 to 28-1/4 after a delayed opening.
